modeSwitching.css: <html data-theme="light|dark">; without it the OS preference is followed
modeSwitching.figma: Set the Color collection mode on a frame

rules.rule: Use roles, never shades or hex.
rules.why: Roles carry the Light and Dark values and the contrast promise; `color.<hue>.<grade>` and hex codes carry neither.

rules.rule: Put text, icons and outlines only on backgrounds listed for them in the pair contract.
rules.why: Only listed pairs are measured. Anything else is unsupported.

rules.rule: On a solid fill (bg.brand, bg.danger, action.primary.bg …) use its partner on- colour.
rules.why: Any other text on a solid fill falls far below 4.5 : 1.

rules.rule: Never use colour alone to carry meaning.
rules.why: Status needs words or an icon, links need an underline, changes need an arrow or sign.

rules.rule: Positive and negative mean good and bad, not up and down.
rules.why: A falling error rate is positive (green with ▼). Choose by meaning; the arrow shows direction.

rules.rule: Hover with translucent tints only on canvas, surface or sunken; inside menus, popovers, dialogs and raised cards use the solid item roles.
rules.why: In Dark, lightening a high surface closes the gap to its text (brand text measured at 2.8 : 1).

rules.rule: Never place ghost buttons or brand-coloured text on a tinted sunken well.
rules.why: Brand text there lands on the 4.5 : 1 line — too close to rely on.
Two primaries force people to choose between equals.

rules.rule: Every focusable element shows a 2px border.focus ring with a 2px gap on :focus-visible. Never remove it.
rules.why: Keyboard users lose their place without it.

rules.rule: Outlines that identify a control use border.input or border.strong; border.subtle and border.default are decorative only.
rules.why: People need to see a field's edge to find it (3 : 1).

rules.rule: Disabled colours are exempt from contrast, so never put information in disabled text; explain nearby why something is disabled.
rules.why: Low-contrast text is hard to read for many people.

rules.rule: Overlays (menus, popovers, dialogs) take their whole elevation level — bg.surface-overlay, border.floating at border.width.line and the level's shadow; modal dialogs also get bg.scrim (Elevation rulebook).
rules.why: Depth must not rely on shadow alone.

rules.rule: Use chart series in order (chart-1, chart-2 …) and label series directly or with a legend.
rules.why: The order is tuned so neighbours stay distinct for colour-blind readers.

rules.rule: Brand colour is identity, not an intent. Never use it to mean success.
rules.why: Intent colours must keep one meaning everywhere.

rules.rule: Design once with roles; switch Light and Dark by mode (data-theme on <html>), never by swapping names.
rules.why: Roles are remapped per mode; swapping names breaks the pair contract.

decisions.question: Where does it sit?
answers: Set back inside a card (table head, well, code)
Stays above scrolling content (sticky header, toolbar)

decisions.question: How important is it?
answers: A good / bad change (with an arrow)

decisions.question: Does it carry meaning?
answers: Inside a button with a label
An icon-only button (toolbar, row actions): ghost button with a neutral icon

decisions.question: Would someone miss the control if this line disappeared?
What is underneath?
answers: Inside a menu, popover, dialog or raised card

roles.name: color.bg.surface-raised
roles.use: Sticky bars: headers, toolbars, sticky table headers (elevation.sticky)

roles.name: color.bg.surface-overlay
roles.use: Menus, popovers, toasts, dialogs (elevation.floating and elevation.modal)

roles.name: color.bg.disabled
roles.use: Disabled control fill (exempt from contrast, WCAG 1.4.3 exception)

roles.name: color.bg.brand
roles.use: Solid brand fill (grade 60) — text on it uses color.fg.on-brand

roles.name: color.bg.success
roles.use: Solid success fill (grade 60) — text on it uses color.fg.on-success

roles.name: color.bg.warning
roles.use: Solid warning fill (grade 25) — text on it uses color.fg.on-warning

roles.name: color.bg.danger
roles.use: Solid danger fill (grade 60) — text on it uses color.fg.on-danger

roles.name: color.bg.info
roles.use: Solid info fill (grade 60) — text on it uses color.fg.on-info

roles.name: color.fg.success
roles.use: Success text and icons — with words or an icon, never colour alone

roles.name: color.fg.warning
roles.use: Warning text and icons — with words or an icon, never colour alone

roles.name: color.fg.danger
roles.use: Danger text and icons — with words or an icon, never colour alone

roles.name: color.fg.info
roles.use: Info text and icons — with words or an icon, never colour alone

roles.name: color.fg.disabled
roles.use: Disabled text (exempt from contrast, WCAG 1.4.3 exception)

roles.name: color.border.subtle
roles.use: Decorative dividers (not needed to identify a control)

roles.name: color.border.floating
roles.use: The edge of anything that floats over content: menus, popovers, toasts, dialogs, a dragged item — seen against every surface below it, kept in forced colours

roles.name: color.border.selected
roles.use: Selected or current item: the border of a selected option or card, the bar under the current tab — with a second cue (a check mark, bold text)

roles.name: color.border.success
roles.use: Success outline — a field that passed validation

roles.name: color.border.warning
roles.use: Warning outline — a field that needs attention

roles.name: color.border.danger
roles.use: Danger outline — a field in error

roles.name: color.border.info
roles.use: Info outline — a highlighted field or callout

roles.name: color.fg.positive
roles.use: A good change, as text — always with an arrow or sign; colour shows good, the arrow shows direction (WCAG 1.4.1)

roles.name: color.fg.negative
roles.use: A bad change, as text — always with an arrow or sign; colour shows bad, the arrow shows direction (WCAG 1.4.1)

roles.name: color.data.positive
roles.use: Marks for good changes: bars, sparklines, deltas

roles.name: color.data.negative
roles.use: Marks for bad changes: bars, sparklines, deltas

roles.name: color.fg.icon
roles.use: Default icons — same weight as muted text

roles.name: color.fg.icon-subtle
roles.use: Secondary icons (chevrons, decorative glyphs next to a label) — 3:1

roles.name: color.bg.state-hover
roles.use: Hover tint over canvas, surface or sunken

roles.name: color.bg.state-pressed
roles.use: Pressed tint over canvas, surface or sunken

roles.name: color.bg.item-hover
roles.use: Hovered item inside a menu, popover, dialog or raised card

roles.name: color.bg.item-pressed
roles.use: Pressed item inside a menu, popover, dialog or raised card

roles.name: color.action.primary.bg
roles.use: Primary button fill — one per view

roles.name: color.action.primary.fg
roles.use: Label and icon on a primary button

roles.name: color.action.secondary.fg
roles.use: Label and icon on a secondary button

roles.name: color.action.secondary.border
roles.use: Secondary button outline — 3:1, it is what shows the button

roles.name: color.action.ghost.bg
roles.use: Ghost button: no fill until hovered

roles.name: color.action.ghost.bg-hover
roles.use: Ghost button, hovered (state layer; inside menus and dialogs use bg/item-hover)

roles.name: color.action.ghost.bg-pressed
roles.use: Ghost button, pressed (state layer; inside menus and dialogs use bg/item-pressed)

roles.name: color.action.danger.fg
roles.use: Label and icon on a destructive button

roles.name: color.shadow.1
roles.use: Shadow strength 1 of 4 (Light: the shadow itself; Dark: a weak extra cue — height there comes from lighter surfaces)

roles.name: color.shadow.2
roles.use: Shadow strength 2 of 4 (Light: the shadow itself; Dark: a weak extra cue — height there comes from lighter surfaces)

roles.name: color.shadow.3
roles.use: Shadow strength 3 of 4 (Light: the shadow itself; Dark: a weak extra cue — height there comes from lighter surfaces)

roles.name: color.shadow.4
roles.use: Shadow strength 4 of 4 (Light: the shadow itself; Dark: a weak extra cue — height there comes from lighter surfaces)
